background: Unknown budgets remove the budget fractions used by classical Adwords allocation rules. The feedback and truncation convention are part of the model, as is the small-bids limit; guarantees for known budgets or arbitrary bid sizes do not transfer automatically.
short_statement: Determine the optimal randomized competitive ratio for Adwords when advertiser budgets are initially unknown.
full_statement: Advertisers have hidden budgets $B_i>0$. On each adversarially ordered query t, bids $b_{it}$ are revealed and the algorithm irrevocably assigns it to one advertiser or discards it. An assigned advertiser pays the bid truncated at its remaining budget; exhaustion is revealed, but budgets are not available upfront. The benchmark is the integral offline optimum knowing all bids and budgets. Let $\gamma=\max_{i,t}b_{it}/B_i$. Determine the optimal randomized competitive ratio in the small-bids limit $\gamma\to0$, for inputs fixed independently of the algorithm's random choices. This is not a failed-allocation model requiring the entire bid to fit.
open_problem: Determine the optimal small-bid randomized ratio within the reviewed $[0.522,1-1/e]$ bounds; framework-specific barriers do not settle this target.
known_results: Udwani, arXiv:2110.00504v5, Theorem 1, bounds deterministic budget-oblivious algorithms by $1/2$. Theorems 2-3 and Corollary 1 give GPG at least $0.522/(1+\gamma)$, hence $0.522$ in the small-bids limit. The general upper benchmark is $1-1/e$. Liang, Tang, Xu, Zhang, and Zhou, arXiv:2210.10370v2, Theorem 2, bound all Perturbed-Ranking perturbation functions by $1-1/e-0.0003$; the canonical perturbation has upper bound $0.624$. These are framework restrictions, not upper bounds for every randomized budget-oblivious algorithm.

counterexample_rationale: Finite adversarial instances can upper-bound proposed algorithms or refute candidate ratios. Factor-revealing LPs may certify tight examples.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search over small bid/budget instances and randomized perturbation distributions can reveal worst cases and candidate optimal algorithms.

literature.synthesis: The deterministic barrier, randomized achievable guarantee, and perturbation-family barriers answer different questions. No reviewed theorem closes the all-algorithms gap.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Use factor-revealing LPs or adversarial instance search for upper bounds, and optimize randomized perturbation distributions for lower bounds. Small-bid limits may simplify analysis into differential equations.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A claimed ratio must be against the offline optimum that knows both budgets and the entire arrival sequence. The proof must state the budget-feedback model exactly, since learning exact remaining budget, learning only on exhaustion, and observing failed allocations are different information structures. It must also state whether it assumes the small-bids limit; a proof for infinitesimal bids does not automatically imply the same constant for arbitrary bid-to-budget ratios. A randomized lower bound should specify whether the adversary is oblivious or adaptive and should use Yao-style distributions or another rigorous minimax argument. Improvements for known-budget Adwords, stochastic arrivals, online matching without budgets, or deterministic multi-channel matching do not resolve this record unless they are explicitly transferred to the unknown-budget model.
